newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures mixed in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures mixed in quiet trade.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures were mixed in early quiet trade, with many players on hold before Tuesday's Federal Open Market Committee meeting.

Traders said the consensus on the trading floor was for a 25-basis-point rate hike when the Fed's policy-making group meets on Tuesday. A Reuters poll last week showed that 33 of 48 economists at various institutions also predicted at least a 25 basis point tightening, and 29 of 37 economists at primary dealers forecast a hike.
Until Tuesday's FOMC results, stock index futures action will remain muted, traders agreed.
"We're not going to see a real wild range today," one Standard and Poor's 500 futures trader said.
By 0936 CST/1536 GMT, most stock indices had turned lower amid intraday technical selling.
June S&Ps slipped to 790.15 after the initial drift up to 794.90 failed.
"We just ran out of gas there and locals dominated it on the way down," the S&P 500 futures trader said. He noted light commission house selling below 792.50.
Support was now seen at 788.40, the 1-1/2 month low settlement from last Thursday.
Last Friday's Globex low of 787.15 was also support, traders said. Resistance was seen at 793.70, 794.90 and 796.30.
Overall, trade was quiet with players sitting on their hands ahead of Tuesday's FOMC meeting.
One firm pegged June S&P 500 fair value at 7.35 points premium to cash, buy programs at 8.75 points premium to cash or wider and sell programs at 5.90 points premium or narrower.

At 1014 CST/1614 GMT, June S&P 500 futures were 3.25 points lower to 788.50, Nasdaq 100s were 23.25 lower at 799.50, KCBT Value Line futures were down 3.00 points to 705.60, Nikkei 225 index futures fell 540.0 to 18,130 and Midcap 400s fell 1.30 points to 261.20.
